annotations.text: dashboard → create tender (draft) → E-Tender Approval gate → publish → bids close → evaluation & L1 recommendation → L1 Approval gate → award

Split-Award (spec §6.3.4, §9.5, §10.2) — Officer proposes an allocation across vendors at L1 Selection (screen 4), Approving Authority confirms/adjusts it at L1 Approval (screen 5); each vendor gets its own PO data file for its share.

Weighting between price and rating for L1 recommendation now has a concrete illustrative default (spec §9.4 QCBS: 70/30 technical/price for critical Assets, 60/40 for Services) — still to be finalized per category.

"Senior official" now resolved by spec §11.2's value-based matrix: ≤₹1L Procurement Admin, ₹1L–10L Department Head, above ₹10L Finance/Management Committee — bands are illustrative, to be finalized with hospital policy.

master catalog (Module 2) → vendor approval → item/asset/service mapping (matrix overview + per-request approval) → ongoing rating (auto price competitiveness + manual params) — feeds eligibility resolution used by E-Tender Approval

Per spec §12: one reusable override/approval engine, not separate logic per screen. Shown here at Vendor Rating (score override), and consolidated at screen 18 (Override & Exception Approval Queue) across every override type in the spec, each with a distinct Reason Code plus free-text Justification.
register → (wait for Vendor Approval) → browse open tenders (only lines you qualify for) → submit sealed bid (technical + commercial) → track status → awards & POs
PO data export (CSV/XML, traceable, not itself the ERP PO) · full audit trail across every stage above, immutable from normal workflows
Open Tender bypasses eligibility filtering entirely (spec §6.8); the Override Queue is the single engine behind every governed override referenced across every screen above (spec §12)
